name: Cape Town International Airport

runway.v: longest runway 01/19, 3,201 m long and 61 m wide; second runway 16/34, 1,701 m × 46 m

ppr.v: non-scheduled flights that need the main apron must tell the ACSA apron office
ppr.quote: Operators of non-scheduled flights requiring use of the main apron must inform ACSA apron office

noise.v: no jet take-offs from runway/taxiway intersections and no engine run-ups between 2000 and 0400 (AIP times), except in an emergency
noise.quote: No jet aircraft to use RWY/TWY intersection for take off between 2000 to 0400.

notes: AIP South Africa AMDT 4/26 (effective 15 Oct 2026) replaced pages AD 2-FACT-15 to 17 only (AD 2.20-2.22: GA area, helicopters, noise). Coordinates, operator, location, hours, runways, fuel and the non-scheduled apron rule come from the eAIP edition valid from 15 Jan 2022, the newest full page that could be opened; please confirm against the consolidated 'Aerodromes (15_OCT_2026)' PDF on caa.co.za (could not be opened here). ACSA has a runway re-alignment programme at Cape Town, so the runway figures in particular need that check. Customs not recorded: the 2022 page says only 'Services available during scheduled operations', which gives no hours. The 2000-0400 rule covers intersection take-offs and engine run-ups only; it is not a curfew, and the AIP did not say whether the times are UTC or local (UTC+2, no DST). The 2022 AIP lists cargo handling up to a B747 freighter and says aircraft with a wingspan of 52 m or more must use apron taxiways to reach stands. IATA code not stated by the sources read.
